en: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first President of the Philippines, not Jose Rizal.
The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed on June 12, 1898, not July 4.
The Sampaguita is the national flower of the Philippines, not the Waling-waling orchid.
The Senate and House of Representatives form the Legislative branch, not the Executive branch.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the government, not just Tagalog.
Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan to fight Spanish rule, rather than serving as a Spanish general.
The three stars on the Philippine flag represent Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao, not the white triangle.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the two-way videophone, not Alexander Graham Bell's original telephone.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño, not the arrival of Ferdinand Magellan.
The President of the Philippines is limited to a single six-year term, not unlimited terms.
Lapulapu defeated Ferdinand Magellan to resist colonization, rather than welcoming Spanish religious conversion.
National Artist Juan Luna painted the famous Spoliarium, rather than sculpting the masterpiece.
